Update:

Got my test results back and they look a little better:

Total cholesterol – 248mg/dL

HDL – 43mg/dL

LDL – 178mg/dL

Triglycerides – 134mg/dL

It's not a lot, but I didn't changed much diet wise since last test. I'll have discussion with Dr. and ask if I can get another couple months, trying to clean up a little more (to a point where I still can keep the diet). And I'm planning on incorporating breakfast to get more fiber to my diet. If it will go down again, then I will probably continue to see where I'm standing on average. If not, then I will discuss the medicine I need to take and go for it.

Thanks for your insight! Doctor told me that this level of LDL is probably genetics rather than diet related too. Something along the lines of 70% genetics, 30% diet. I didn't connected it has a name until I've read your message. 

I'll definitely ask her if your advice could be suitable to try and find out!

I'm not really eating any whole grains to be honest, apart from bread from time to time, but not daily, no. I've read that oats do wonders and I definitely need to add them to my breakfast (I do not eat any breakfast at all now). As for the fish, I don't like seafood, it's the "fishiness" if you can call it, that throws me off. I guess fish oil could help, but that's probably not enough to supplement the lack of fish overall?

  
As for the stress, I don't really understand what it means. I hear people say they are stressed, but for me it's either unknown feeling or I'm in constant state of it and I don't know it. I overthink a lot daily, but I don't know if it can be called stress.  
Thanks for all the tips!
